nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaching the forest floor and open water drives growth for the swamp and bottomland trees and shrubs.

nodes.name: River flood pulse
nodes.desc: The Pascagoula floods its low forests in the wet season. This moves seeds and nutrients and keeps cypress swamp and bottomland forest wet.

nodes.name: Alluvial soil & nutrients
nodes.desc: River-borne silt and leaf litter build the rich, wet soils of the floodplain.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi and bacteria break down fallen leaves, logs and carcasses in the warm, wet floodplain and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Bald cypress
nodes.desc: A flood-tolerant swamp conifer. Its seeds travel by water, and its seedlings need wet but not drowned soil to start.

nodes.name: Water oak
nodes.desc: A common bottomland oak whose acorns feed deer, squirrels and jays.

nodes.name: Catbrier
nodes.desc: A thorny, tangling vine of woods and thickets whose leaves and berries are eaten by wildlife.

nodes.name: Yaupon
nodes.desc: An evergreen holly shrub of the Gulf coastal plain. Its berries are eaten by birds and mammals.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: The most recorded large herbivore here. It browses leaves, vines and acorns in the bottomlands.

nodes.name: Fox squirrel
nodes.desc: A big tree squirrel that eats nuts, seeds and fruits, and spreads cypress seeds as it chews cones.

nodes.name: Nutria
nodes.desc: An introduced aquatic rodent that eats marsh and swamp plants and clips young cypress seedlings.

nodes.name: Blue Jay
nodes.desc: The most recorded bird in the area. It eats acorns, seeds and insects, and takes eggs and nestlings.

nodes.name: Aquatic insect larvae
nodes.desc: Larvae in the river and bayous eat leaf litter, algae and detritus, and feed fish.

nodes.name: Bluegill
nodes.desc: A common sunfish that eats aquatic insects and is prey for herons, ospreys, otters and alligators.

nodes.name: Raccoon
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats fruit, birds and eggs, small mammals and carrion along the river.

nodes.name: North American river otter
nodes.desc: Eats mainly fish, plus crayfish and frogs. It needs permanent clean water with cover.

nodes.name: Osprey
nodes.desc: A fish-eating hawk that dives feet-first for live fish in the river and nearby coast.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A scavenger that finds carrion by scent and cleans dead deer, raccoons and other animals from the floodplain.

nodes.name: Cottonmouth
nodes.desc: A semi-aquatic pit viper of swamps and sloughs that eats fish, frogs and other small animals.

nodes.name: American alligator
nodes.desc: An opportunistic apex predator of swamps and rivers that eats fish, turtles, raccoons and nutria. Its dug holes hold water in dry spells.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: A stealthy cat that takes rabbits, rodents, squirrels, nutria and deer fawns across the forests.
